summary: Divyaraj Amiya is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He holds posts as a faculty member at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich (both attested 2026).

Diwakar Acharya is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler. His posts include Kyoto University (2006–2016) and a professorship and fellowship at the University of Oxford from 2016.
Dixian (1858–1932) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Mingzu. He served as abbot at Guanzong Temple from around 1913 to 1932.

Dmitry Kudryavsky (1867–1920) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev at St. Petersburg University from around 1886 to 1890 and served at the University of Tartu from around 1898 to 1918.
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Dodrupchen Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught pupils including Ronald M. Davidson and Tulku Thondup.

Dominic Goodall is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at Wolfson College, Oxford, and at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (from 2000).

Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University and the University of Virginia, completing his doctoral studies under David Germano, and held a post at Utah State University (attested 2017).

Dominik Haas works in Indology and religious studies, completing doctoral studies under Marion Rastelli. He has held posts as a DOC Fellow at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia and at the University of Vienna (attested 2022).

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of London and University of Oxford. His posts include the Wellcome Institute (~1985–2007), University College London (2002–2009), University of Vienna (2009–2015), and University of Alberta (from 2015).
Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1979–1984). He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, from around 1987.

Dominique-Sila Khan (1949–2016) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and served as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).
Don A. Pittman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed doctoral studies at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University.

Don Handelman is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester. He served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1972–2007).

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe (1865–1937) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Richmond College, Galle, and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg. He was epigraphist for the Government of Ceylon (~1899–1929) and taught at the University of London (~1918–1930).

Donald A. Ringe is a linguist who earned his PhD at Yale University under Warren Crawford Cowgill. He taught classics at Bard College (1983–1985) before joining the linguistics faculty at the University of Pennsylvania in 1985.

Donald E. Gjertson is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Ching-yu Wang and held a faculty post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst from around 1976 to 2007.

Donald Eric Capps (1939–2015) was a religious studies scholar educated at Lewis & Clark College, Yale, and the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago, UNC Charlotte, and Phillips University, and was a professor at Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).
Donald Harper is a sinologist who held posts at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and the University of Chicago, where he served as Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies (attested 2026).

Donald K. Swearer is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar mentored by Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Singkha Wannasai. He held posts at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004) and Harvard University (2004–2010).
